newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA gold sales to add total A$2.4 bln to exports.
newsitem.headline: RBA gold sales to add total A$2.4 bln to exports.

text.p: The balance of proceeds from the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) sale of its gold reserves will boost exports by a total of A$600 million in August and September, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
Including the A$1.8 billion proceeds of the gold delivered in June, the RBA sales of 167 million tonnes of gold announced earlier this month would have boosted exports by a total of A$2.4 billion.
The ABS said the gold sales would be recorded as exports of goods in June, August and September in line with the delivery arrangements established for the sales.

The sale of the RBA gold would not be reflected in the ABS business stocks (inventories) publication as that covered private business, the ABS said, although its impact on the national accounts would be balanced out.
"In the domestic production account, the contribution made to net exports by the gold transactions will be exactly offset by a decrease in stocks, thereby having no impact on GDP," the ABS said.

For the international investment postion statistics, which includes net foreign debt, the ABS said that in addition to the transaction and non-transaction entries noted for offical reserve assets in the balance of payments, the decline in gold reserves would be shown as an "other change" (non-transaction) in levels.

Each of the gold sales was being treated by the ABS as an extreme irregular event and so was included in the seasonally adjusted trade balance series but without the application of seasonal factors to the export values, and was excluded from the trend series.

Although the gold was sold under forward contracts, the ABS said it showed up in the balance of payment statistics as exports at the time the goods changed ownership, which was when the gold was delivered, not when the contract to sell was entered into.

As the gold used to meet the June delivery commitments was held overseas, it did not cross the Australian customs frontiers and therefore there was no entry in the ABS international merchandise trade statistics on a recorded trade basis, the bureau said.
